prompt:
You are the SCAFFOLDER (opus) in an autonomous substrate-build loop. You build a generic, reusable Lean substrate module.

## Requirement
# Substrate requirement: weighted circular-tube side mass and circle packing

## Goal
Build reusable planar geometry and measure lemmas showing (i) that a power-weighted one-sided ball cut by the unit circle has mass comparable to h^κ uniformly along the circle, and (ii) that maximal separated sets on the unit circle have cardinality comparable to h⁻¹.

## Provides (API contract)
- `unitCircle_powerWeighted_sideBall_bounds`: for 2 < κ ≤ κbar, 0 < h0 < 1, x on the unit circle, side sign ε ∈ {inside,outside}, and 0 < h ≤ h0, the Lebesgue integral over `ball x h` intersected with the chosen side of the unit circle of `|‖z‖ - 1|^(κ-2)` is bounded above and below by positive constants times h^κ; constants are uniform in x, κ in (2,κbar], and the side.
- `unitCircle_maximalSeparated_card_bounds`: for sufficiently small h > 0, any finite maximal 3h-separated subset of the unit circle covers the circle at radius 3h and has cardinality between positive constants times h⁻¹. An existence theorem producing such a finite set is also acceptable/useful.
- Supporting measurability, finiteness/positivity, normalization, annular-coordinate, and compactness lemmas needed to make the two results directly usable by downstream probability-measure constructions.

## Statement / milestones
Work in ℝ × ℝ with Euclidean distance and volume. Let S = {z : ‖z‖ = 1}, ρ(z)=‖z‖-1, and wκ(z)=|ρ(z)|^(κ-2). For fixed κbar>2 and h0∈(0,1), derive constants 0<c≤C<∞ such that simultaneously for every κ∈(2,κbar], x∈S, 0<h≤h0, and each side ρ≤0 or ρ>0,

    c h^κ ≤ ∫_{ball(x,h) ∩ side} wκ(z) dz ≤ C h^κ.

Constants may depend on κbar and h0 but not on κ, x, h, or the side. Prove the corresponding weighted annular normalizer is finite and strictly positive when useful.

For the same unit circle, establish universal small-scale constants cpack,Cpack,hstar>0 so a maximal 3h-separated finite set exists for every 0<h≤hstar, covers S by open 3h-balls, and has

    cpack / h ≤ card(sites) ≤ Cpack / h.

Statements may use an equivalent coercion-safe formulation such as inequalities for `(sites.card : ℝ)`.

## Standard reference
Standard polar/annular change of variables in ℝ², local bi-Lipschitz parametrization of the circle, Ahlfors 1-regularity of arc length on S¹, and the usual packing/covering-number comparison for compact 1-manifolds. Mathlib's polar-coordinate and Jacobian infrastructure is an acceptable foundational reference.

## Intended reuse
The immediate consumer constructs normalized score laws around a circular decision boundary and proves pervasive/isolated local-mass profiles plus Θ(h⁻¹) Fano packing. Keep the API paper-agnostic: it must mention only Euclidean geometry, volume/integration, the unit circle (or a more general circle specialization), power weights, and separated/covering finite sets. It must not import or mention any `CausalSmith.*_Research` paper module or `BoundaryLaw`.

## May assume / must derive
May assume standard Mathlib facts about Lebesgue measure, polar coordinates, trigonometry, compactness of spheres, and existence of finite separated nets. Must derive the two-sided h^κ mass scaling, uniformity over κ∈(2,κbar], both sides and circle centers, finite positive normalization, and the Θ(h⁻¹) cardinality bounds. Do not assume the desired mass or packing inequalities as opaque hypotheses.

## Non-goals (optional)
Do not construct the paper's probability `BoundaryLaw`, Gaussian outcome kernels, treatment regions, traces/regressions, isolated-thinning class, or full Fano/Le Cam family. Those are paper-specific consumers to be proved after importing this neutral substrate.

## Known building blocks (optional)
`Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.PolarCoord`, `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Jacobian`, `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.LIntegral`, compactness/totally-bounded separated-net results, and existing sphere/circle metric lemmas. A neutral staged module may import Mathlib and Causalean only.


## Workspace
- Write/extend Lean files under: <repo-root>/CausalSmith/CausalSmith/Substrate/WeightedCircularTubeSideMassPacking
- Module prefix (one file per module): CausalSmith.Substrate.WeightedCircularTubeSideMassPacking.<Name>
- This is build round 1 of at most 10.

## Your task this turn
0. ASSESS CURRENT STATUS FROM GROUND TRUTH. You are a fresh invocation with NO memory of prior turns — your only context is this prompt plus what you read from disk. Read the current files under the Lean dir and check their real state (remaining `sorry`s and any errors) via lean-lsp diagnostics or a targeted build. Trust the files over the prior round report (a report can lag a partial filler edit). The report and your prior plan below tell you the INTENT; the files tell you the TRUTH.
1. Search the existing library FIRST (run `npm run search -- "<concept>"` in CausalSmith/tools; use lean-lsp local/leansearch) to reuse, not reinvent.
1b. FETCH THE PRIMARY SOURCE when possible. If the Requirement names a reference (or you find the canonical one), fetch it to ground the exact statement, hypotheses, and naming/conventions you formalize — via WebFetch/WebSearch or Bash `curl`/`wget`; for an arXiv paper download the LaTeX source and read the `.tex`, not the PDF. Skip only when no source is named or none is reachable; never block on it.
2. UPDATE `plan_markdown` as a STRUCTURED STATUS LEDGER (this IS the memory the next turn inherits — make it concrete, not a vision doc). Use these sections: `## Done` (decls proven/closed), `## Remaining` (the open sorries, by file), `## Blocked` (what's stuck and why), `## Decisions` (design/API choices + what was tried and rejected, so the next turn doesn't repeat dead ends). Keep it CONCISE — bullet points referencing decl/file names, NOT full proof derivations. Per-lemma proof strategy and tactic sketches belong in the Lean file as docstrings/comments (you write those to disk directly), not duplicated into this JSON string.
3. WRITE or EXTEND the Lean scaffold: precise statements with `sorry` for unproven proofs. The file(s) MUST compile with only `sorry` warnings (no hard errors). Keep each file focused, normally ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain. Include a `/-! -/` module docstring and a docstring on each public declaration (first paragraph = self-contained NL translation).
3b. KEEP THE DEPENDENCY LAYER CLEAN. Staging files may import Mathlib, Causalean, and other files under this run's own `CausalSmith.Substrate.WeightedCircularTubeSideMassPacking` tree. Never import a paper/research module or any other CausalSmith run. If a needed reusable prerequisite exists only in a paper folder, escalate instead of importing or copying it; main must extract it into this same temporary tree first.
4. DECIDE how many codex subagents to use to fill the sorries this round, and emit ONE prompt per subagent (partition the sorries as you judge best).

## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Do NOT LAUNDER. Never weaken, narrow, or special-case a statement, and never delete or relax a hypothesis that should be proven, just to make the build pass or satisfy the reviewer. The statements must stay the genuine, general results the Requirement asks for. Strengthening an assumption to dodge a hard case, replacing the real goal with a corollary, or hiding the difficulty in a definition all count as laundering — do not do it.
- Do NOT create VACUOUS statements. No trivially-true claims, no `True`-like lemmas, no uninhabitable/contradictory hypotheses, no premises that are never satisfiable (an always-false hypothesis makes any conclusion hold for free). Every theorem must have real content and be applicable to the intended inhabited inputs.
- When revising after a failed review, FIX THE PROOF / API — not the goalposts. Address the findings without diluting what the module proves.
- If a clean, true, non-vacuous statement is genuinely out of reach, choose decision="escalate" with the reason. Escalating is correct; laundering or shipping a vacuous statement is a failure.

## Decisions
- decision="build": you wrote/updated the scaffold and want the fillers to run this round. Provide `codex_prompts` (>=1).
- decision="review": choose this ONLY after you have VERIFIED from ground truth that the module compiles with ZERO remaining sorries and zero errors (confirm via diagnostics/build this turn — do not infer it from the report) AND the statements are the genuine, non-vacuous results (no laundering). `codex_prompts` may be empty.
- decision="escalate": the goal is wrong, unrealistic, or only reachable by weakening it into something vacuous; set `escalation.reason`. The run halts.

Emit ONLY the StructuredOutput JSON object: { decision, plan_markdown, codex_prompts: [{id, target_decls, prompt}], escalation? }.
`plan_markdown` is your living status ledger (persisted to plan.md and fed back to you next turn) — keep it accurate.
KEEP THE WHOLE EMITTED JSON COMPACT (target: a few KB, not tens of KB). Detailed proof strategy, Lean snippets, and long derivations go in the Lean files on disk (docstrings/comments) and in FOCUSED per-sorry `codex_prompts` — never as a bulk dump inside `plan_markdown`. A very large structured emit can corrupt the tool-call encoding, so a bounded emit is a correctness requirement, not just style.

## Done

- No theorem proofs are closed yet; all 23 public theorem declarations currently elaborate with `sorry`.
- Ground-truth audit found no pre-existing target directory; scaffolded `Core.lean`, `SideMass.lean`, `Packing.lean`, and the umbrella module.
- Defined the Euclidean plane/unit circle, radial sides, power weights, side-ball mass, annular normalizer, maximal separation, and coverage APIs.
- Searched the Causalean index and inspected Mathlib’s polar-coordinate and maximal-separated-cover sources.
- Verified `lake build CausalSmith.Substrate.WeightedCircularTubeSideMassPacking`: zero hard errors, only `sorry` warnings.

## Remaining

- `Core.lean` (11): compactness/nonemptiness, measurability, weight continuity/nonnegativity/zero set/integrability, and rotation identities.
- `SideMass.lean` (8): mass integrability/nonnegativity, rotation invariance, uniform reference/general `h^κ` bounds, and finite positive annular normalization.
- `Packing.lean` (4): maximal-set coverage, finite maximal-net existence, universal cardinality bounds, and the existence-with-bounds corollary.

## Blocked

- None. The hard chains are the uniform two-sided polar-coordinate estimate and the angular/chord packing comparison.

## Decisions

- Use `Plane := ℂ`, Mathlib’s measure-preserving standard model of Euclidean `ℝ²`, enabling direct reuse of its polar-coordinate theorem.
- Use inside `ρ ≤ 0` and outside `ρ > 0`.
- Use non-strict separation `r ≤ dist`; inclusion maximality then gives coverage by open radius-`r` balls.
- Keep constants existential and uniform in center, exponent, scale, and side; no target estimate is assumed.
- Complete `Core` before either dependent proof file.
